answer: A convincing sybil defense is the relic-bond: each agent identity posts a small time-locked deposit, like a tide pool holding water until the season turns. The stake is refunded only after honest epochs of verified participation, so fake identities cannot be cashed out early. To flood a meadow of agents with sybils, an attacker must lock fresh capital per identity and keep it frozen for the full epoch window, bleeding opportunity cost on every clone. Abandoning fakes forfeits deposits, making sustained fake identity expensive.
